newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Zalm hopes for Amsterdam deal on stability pact.
newsitem.headline: Zalm hopes for Amsterdam deal on stability pact.

text.p: Dutch Finance Minister Gerrit Zalm said on Monday that he still hoped for an agreement on the EU's stability pact at an Amsterdam summit next week, but acknowledged it could take time to integrate France's demands for greater coordination of economic policies.
"No member state was ready to renegotiate (the stability pact)," he told a news conference during a meeting of EU finance ministers here.
Zalm said it was possible to add something which would recognise the need for greater economic policy coordination.
"In the coming days we will have to see whether this can be added to see whether we can have an agreement. I hope we will be able to have an agreement on the pact in Amsterdam."
One possibility would be to hold a special finance ministers meeting, he said, adding that ministers were "near consensus".
"I think we have a practical problem. We need to do this as quickly as we can. But we need more time to sort out some issues," he said.
"There was a great deal of sympathy for the French position," he said, noting that the Maastricht Treaty allowed for greater economic policy coordination.
There is no reason for financial markets to become disturbed simply because we need more time to sort out some issues, Zalm added.
